text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish chemical firm Boryszew SA, buoyed by auto industry demand but hurt by a relatively low level of exports, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report.
"The percentage of production directed for export, which is more profitable than domestic sales, is too small," the report dated November 29 but released on Monday said.
On that day Boryszew closed on the Warsaw bourse at 29.1 zlotys and closed at 28.7 zlotys on Tuesday December 24, the last session before the Christmas break.
Handlowy said Boryszew should be helped by increasing long-term demand from the construction industry and its strong market share in its core products of anti-freezes and softening agents.
But it said a bad sign was the company's dependence on the Zaklady Azotowe Kedzierzyn SA nitrogen producer and Petrochemia Plock SA refinery, which are competitors as well as suppliers.
Handlowy said Boryszew was also exposed to seasonal sales and price fluctuations of raw materials.
It predicted the firm would lift net profit to 8.5 million zlotys this year and 10.2 million next year from 6.9 million in 1995.
It said sales would rise to 120 million zlotys this year and 140 million next year from 116 million in 1995.
